Re-verified at source: the 10-Q note (XBRL R21) shows the 2026 program raised from $14.6B to $18.2B on 2026-04-23 and $8.5B remaining at 2026-07-17; the cover shows 1,072,671,613 shares; the next dividend is $1.17 (record 2026-11-25). H2-2026 buybacks = $8.5B - Sept dividend ($1.02 x ~1,072M = $1.09B) - Dec dividend ($1.17 x ~1,055M = $1.23B) = ~$6.2B, about 38M shares at an assumed ~$163 average. 2027: $30.0B - $18.2B = $11.8B, less ~$4.8B of dividends (4 x $1.17 x ~1,030M) = ~$7.0B of buybacks, ~77% ($5.4B) by Oct 9, about 35M shares at ~$155. Add ~4.6M of net equity-comp issuance (10-Q equity statement: 2,699,892 RSUs vested less 862,204 withheld = 1.84M net in H1 2026, x 2.5 half-years to Oct 2027) and ~0.6M of dilutive securities (Q2 diluted 1,082,409,636 less basic 1,081,771,279 weighted shares): 1,072.7 - 38 - 35 + 4.6 + 0.6 = ~1,005M. I do not round up: spectrum spending could cut buybacks, but the Feb 2026 8-K also has a 'flexible envelope of over $22.0 billion' that can go to additional stockholder returns, so the risks are two-sided. One correction: agent_5 says the 10-Q states the ~$30B covers Jan 2026 to end-2027 including the $18.2B program. Note 12 (R21) does not say that. The Feb 2026 8-K says 'over $50.0 billion remains of the $80.0 billion capital envelope ... currently including up to approximately $30.0 billion for stockholder returns' through 2027. Reading the $30B as covering 2026-27 is a reasonable inference, not a stated fact. The whole 1,005-1,020M range moves value by only ~$2.4 a share.

disagreements.topic: Net debt at the horizon: held flat vs re-levered to 2.3x
disagreements.positions: agent_1, agent_2 and agent_4 hold company-basis net debt flat at $84.1B plus $3.46B towers. agent_3 re-levers to 2.3x LTM EBITDA ($89.1B), as the round-1 supervisor did. agent_5 holds StockAnalysis-basis claims flat at $117.6B (including leases).
disagreements.resolution: Held flat at $84.1B plus $3.46B towers (company basis). The cash arithmetic supports it. AFCF from Jul 2026 to Sep 2027 is ~$23.8B: H2 2026 = $18.6B guide midpoint - $9.396B H1 AFCF = ~$9.2B, plus 0.75 x ~$19.5B for 2027 = ~$14.6B. Returns over the same period, capped by the authorized envelope, are ~$18.0B ($8.5B + $0.39B in H2 2026, plus ~77% of $11.8B = $9.1B in 2027). That leaves ~$5.8B for spectrum and other uses without new borrowing. Re-levering to 2.3x while also capping buybacks at the envelope double-penalizes: it adds ~$5.3B of debt that buys neither shares nor anything in horizon EBITDA. Leverage drifts to ~2.2x, below the 2.5x target in the Feb 2026 8-K. Downside sensitivity: if spectrum spending does push net debt to 2.3x, the EV leg loses ~$5.3 a share and the blend ~$1.6.

one_month_reasoning: I keep the forecasters' mean 1-month ladder (median just above $148.58, monthly sigma ~10.5%). Every event in the window is now verified at source: AT&T Q3 before the open on Oct 21, Verizon Q3 on Oct 26, the FOMC on Oct 27-28 with the 10-year at 5.22%, and T-Mobile's Q3 at ~4:05pm ET on Oct 28. The Q3 guide (~250k adds, EBITDA +8%, service revenue +6%) is confirmed in the Q2 call transcript and largely priced. The FCC Oct-29 item stays out, being unconfirmed.
confidence_reason: The round-2 forecasts converged (fair values $159.6-166, mean $163.1; thesis breaks $115-118), but they rested on aggregator peer multiples. Rebuilt from filings and consensus, the peer medians are lower (P/E 9.50x vs 9.95x; EV/EBITDA 6.53x vs 7.38x) and TMUS's own premium to them is larger, so the reconciled fair value is $155.0, about 5% below the agents' mean. I scaled the forecasters' mean ladder by that ratio (155.0/163.0) rather than rebuild each agent's mixture; that is a mechanical correction, not new information.
thesis_break_reason: $115 is ~8.0x the verified FY2027 consensus EPS of $14.44 (StockAnalysis, non-GAAP), at Verizon's 7.98x NTM P/E rebuilt from its Oct 9 close and consensus ($41.65 / $5.22). It is also a ~15.8% yield on the low end of 2027 AFCF guidance per current share ($19.5B / 1,072.7M = $18.18). A sustained trade there would mean the market has abandoned both the growth premium and the 2027 framework. Likely causes: the $40-41B EBITDA / $19.5-20.5B AFCF targets cut at the Feb 2027 guide (first under the new CFO), account adds well below the 950k-1.05M 2026 guide after the Q3 churn bump, or SpaceX securing an MVNO or terrestrial route to scale before its H1-2028 target. It is ~23% below spot, about 0.8-0.9 sigma at 27-30% vol.
key_drivers: The 2027 framework is intact on paper and the Q3 guide still shows operating leverage. Targets: Core Adj. EBITDA $40.0-41.0B, AFCF $19.5-20.5B (Feb 2026 8-K), maintained on Sept 3. Q3 guide: EBITDA ~$9.4B (+8.3%) on service revenue ~$19.3B (+5.8%) (Q2 call; Q2 Factbook bases). I haircut 2027 EBITDA by only 1.5% ($39.4B).

Valuation is undemanding: 10.3x FY2027 consensus EPS ($148.58 / $14.44; 10.63x NTM) and an 11.54% trailing FCF yield, between T (11.60%) and VZ (12.44%), despite a 17.03% 3Y EPS growth forecast vs 6.99% (VZ) and 11.06% (T). I give it +8% to the 9.50x filings-based core peer median (10.25x).

Buybacks within an authorized envelope: $8.5B left in the $18.2B 2026 program at 2026-07-17 (10-Q R21) and up to ~$30B of returns through 2027 (Feb 2026 8-K) take the count to ~1,005M by Oct 2027 with net debt flat at $84.1B (leverage drifts to ~2.2x vs a 2.5x target).

SpaceX is a multiple overhang, not a P&L event, within the horizon. The Grain 800 MHz deal (up to 14 MHz paired) needs FCC approval and is not compatible with V1/V2 satellites. The SpaceX CFO targets mobile service in H1 2028, and SpaceX is undecided on building its own network or partnering with carriers (Light Reading).
Rates and the near-term tape: the 10-year was 5.22% on 2026-10-08 (FRED). Q3 on Oct 28 comes 48 hours after the FOMC and after the AT&T and Verizon prints, so the 1-month distribution is wide.

fair_value.reason: Value at 2027-10-09, before ~$4.7 of dividends; every method is an estimate built on inputs re-opened at source, with the peer multiples rebuilt from filings and consensus by the citation gate (2026-10-12). (1) P/E, weight 0.4: FY2027 consensus $14.44 (StockAnalysis, non-GAAP adjusted). FY2028 = 14.44 x 1.10 = $15.88. Oct-2027 NTM = 0.25 x 14.44 + 0.75 x 15.88 = $15.52, less 3% = $15.05 (the 3% matches my EBITDA haircut: a $0.6B shortfall is ~$0.45B after tax, or ~$0.45 a share, ~3% of $14.44). x 10.25x (+8% on the 9.50x core NTM median) = $154.3. (2) EV/EBITDA, weight 0.3: 2027 Core Adj. EBITDA $39.4B ($40.0B low end less 1.5%). Horizon LTM = 0.25 x 37.3 + 0.75 x 39.4 = $38.875B. Multiple 6.14x on the company basis (core peer median 6.53x x 1.05 = 6.86x on the lease-inclusive peer basis, / 1.118, where 1.118 = TMUS 7.69x on that basis [(159.38 + 86.92 debt + 3.461 towers + 29.058 operating leases - 2.825 cash) / 35.902] / 6.878x on the company basis [(159.38 + 84.095 + 3.461) / 35.902]). EV $238.6B - $84.095B net debt (held flat) - $3.461B towers = $151.1B / 1,005M = $150.3. (3) FCF yield, weight 0.3: horizon LTM AFCF = 0.25 x $18.6B (2026 guide midpoint) + 0.75 x $19.1B (2027 estimate) = $18.975B / 1,005M = $18.88 at 11.75% = $160.7. Blend: 0.4 x 154.3 + 0.3 x 150.3 + 0.3 x 160.7 = 61.7 + 45.1 + 48.2 = $155.0. Versus the agents ($159.6-166, mean $163.1) it is lower because their P/E and EV/EBITDA anchors were aggregator figures; on filed data the peer medians are lower and TMUS's current premium larger. Sensitivities: each 10M shares is ~$1.5 a share on the EV and FCF legs (~$0.9 on the blend); net debt at 2.3x is -$1.6 on the blend; +/-0.25x on the P/E is +/-$1.5 on the blend; +/-0.25x on the peer-basis EV/EBITDA is +/-$2.6 on the blend.

summary: TMUS sits at $148.58 after a 13.3% drop on SpaceX's Grain 800 MHz deal, a threat whose service launch is targeted for H1 2028, after the horizon.
